summary: William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge (~1921–1925) and taught John Crook. He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1932 to 1969.

William James was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Plymouth College, Harvard University, and Harvard Medical School, he held posts at Harvard as lecturer (1872), assistant professor (1876, 1880), and professor (1885).

William Jones was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harrow, Oxford, Middle Temple, and under teachers including Mirza, Ramachandra, and Ramalocana. He served as Puisne and Chief Justice at Fort William and founded The Asiatic Society (1784).

William L. Ames works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned an M.S. from Caltech and a Ph.D. from the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as a librarian at John F. Kennedy University.

William M. Bodiford is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale (Ph.D. under Stanley Weinstein) and became a professor at UCLA circa 1992 after teaching at Davidson and Iowa.

William M. Gorvine specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Connecticut College (B.A.) and the University of Virginia (M.A., Ph.D.), completing his doctorate under David Germano alongside teachers such as Jeffrey Hopkins.

William Magee specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held a professorship there (attested 1992), and taught Tibetan Buddhism at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2008).

William Muir was a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kilmarnock Academy, Haileybury (~1835–1837), and the University of Edinburgh. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Edinburgh (~1885–1903).
William P. Chu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his MA at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2006 and conducted doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

William Price was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary and served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College from circa 1813 to 1830.

William R. Hutchison was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Oxford and Yale. He held posts at Yale, Hunter College, American University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison before joining Harvard University in 1968.

William R. LaFleur specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago (Ph.D.), he held faculty posts at Princeton (~1971–1978), UCLA (~1978–1990), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–2010).

William Rainey Harper was a linguist who studied at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He served as professor at Yale (1886) and became the founding president and department head at the University of Chicago (1891–1906).
William Robertson was a historian who studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh (1733–1741). He later served as the Principal of the University of Edinburgh starting in 1762.

William Roxburgh, active in Indology, studied medicine at Edinburgh under John Hope and Alexander Monro, and at Marischal College. He served as superintendent of Samalkot Garden (1781) and head of the Indian Botanic Garden (1793).

William S.-Y. Wang is a linguist and sinologist who studied at Columbia and Michigan. He held faculty posts at UC Berkeley (1966–1994), City University of Hong Kong (1996–2004), and The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (~2004–2016).
William Stede was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held an academic post at SOAS and the University of London from circa 1928 to 1949.

William Van Gordon is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. Attested in 2015, he worked as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

William Ward was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Ewood Hall Theological Academy under John Fawcett in 1797. He served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission (~1800–1823) and co-founded Serampore College in 1818.

William Wilson Hunter was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887) and as vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta in 1886.
